title: Gates write tmp/<command>/ and nothing ignores it, so a consumer's tree reads dirty after its first check
body:
## Problem

Every sealed gate writes its logs under `tmp/<command>/` (`open_run_log`, `lib/runlog:230`, through `gate_out_dir`), and nothing in devbin arranges for that directory to be ignored: no code in install, upgrade or doctor mentions ignore state. In a consumer whose `.gitignore` does not cover `tmp/`, the first `check` leaves an untracked `tmp/` in `git status`, and from then on `git_head_identity` counts it (`lib/helpers:2121-2138`), so `--version` and fullcycle's header report the tree `+dirty`. Only the release pre-flight knows (`lib/cmd/release:570-578`), and it probes `tmp/release` alone, so a project that ignores only that path passes the pre-flight and then fails at step 5, "a gate changed the tree" (`lib/cmd/release:707-721`), after step 4 has committed. Parked at the 0.1.8 cut, from a consumer's cut; fixed forward in the bundle on hv's word, 2026-10-03.

## Measured at 2ce9411 (0152 v1 on 953d040; cc's evidence pass)

A fresh `install --name demo`, committed, with no `.gitignore`: after `check all`, `git status` shows `?? tmp/` (14 files under `-uall`), `git check-ignore tmp/check` exits 1, and `--version` moves from `(<sha>)` to `(<sha> +dirty)`.

## Fix (for vc's review)

The output directory ignores itself: where `open_run_log` creates `tmp/<command>/`, one helper beside `gate_out_dir` writes `*` to `tmp/<command>/.gitignore` when that file is absent, and never at or above the project root. A write that fails warns naming the path, and the seal is still written. That is a file inside devbin's own output directory, not the project's `.gitignore`, so the release core's standing choice not to write the project's `.gitignore` stands; the pre-flight calls the same helper before it probes, so `--dry-run` and the real cut agree. Measured: with `tmp/check/.gitignore` holding `*`, `tmp/` drops out of `git status`. The fallback, if writing into the tree is ruled out, is `doctor` naming the gap and install's closing lines saying it.

## Done when

1. In a fixture with no `.gitignore`, a gate run leaves `git status` empty and `--version` without `+dirty`; red at 2ce9411.
2. A line in the project's own `.gitignore` survives every gate run, and no `.gitignore` is written at or above the project root.
3. The release pre-flight and step 5 agree on a project that ignores nothing.

## Resolution

Fixed at 430e2c28. Every gate's log directory ignores itself: before the first log lands, `*` is written into `tmp/<command>/.gitignore`, devbin's own output directory, never the project's `.gitignore`. Only a directory strictly inside `tmp/`, resolved physically, gets one: never `tmp/` itself, never through a link out of the tree, never where a `.gitignore` already is, and never in a directory git tracks, or where git cannot say. The release pre-flight asks the same rule without writing, so a dry run and a cut reach the same verdict.

Against the done-when list:

1. In a fixture with no `.gitignore`, a gate run leaves `git status` empty and `--version` without `+dirty`: runlog.bats's first arm, red on the code beneath this change.
2. A `.gitignore` the project made in a log directory is left exactly as it was, and none is written at or above the root or in `tmp/` itself: two arms, the first held by a mutant since the base wrote nothing.
3. The release pre-flight and step 5 agree on a project that ignores nothing: releasecut.bats's arm, where `--dry-run` and the cut both pass step 2 and the cut finds no dirt at step 5; red on the first version, whose dry run refused.

Evidence. 10 mutants, all killed. The arms run green under GNU coreutils, findutils and sed as well as the BSD tools. The full suite on the landing tree: on main 962e0daf with 0157 v2.1, 0158 v2.2 and 0156 v2.1 applied in that order, in a fresh clone: 2159 of 2159 ok, 0 not ok, its .errors empty (seal 20261005-1749), 17:49:31Z to 18:37:10Z; 5 skipped, the same five as cc's.
